idiom_name: SessionManager + SessionStore over OpenSSL and Asio/Boost.Beast
implementation_notes: C++ has no standard session type; the realization is a SessionManager owning a SessionStore (std::unordered_map behind a std::shared_mutex for one process, or a Redis client for several) and a transport layer writing Set-Cookie on an Asio/Boost.Beast response. Identifiers come from RAND_bytes, records hold the principal and expiry timestamps, lookup validates and refreshes last-use, invalidation erases the record. Because no single web framework dominates C++, the classic structure remains justified here; framework stacks such as Drogon or oatpp supply their own session facility when adopted, in which case only the policy calls (regenerate on login, invalidate on logout, timeout configuration) remain.
pitfalls: Erasing from an unordered_map while other threads hold iterators or references invalidates them; hand out std::shared_ptr sessions and erase under the exclusive lock.
A shared_ptr held by a request handler keeps a revoked session alive in memory and can serve one more request unless handlers re-check the store.
Hand-built Set-Cookie strings are an attribute-injection path; build them through the framework's cookie type and reject control characters.
